newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-RANATUNGA LEADS SRI LANKA TO COMFORTABLE WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RANATUNGA LEADS SRI LANKA TO COMFORTABLE WIN.

text.p: Arjuna Ranatunga produced a classic captain's innings to lead Sri Lanka to a comfortable six-wicket win in their one-day match against Central Districts on Thursday.

Ranatunga finished unbeaten on 96 when he ended the match 6.3 overs early by hitting a six off Central Districts captain Mark Greatbatch to see his side safely past the home team's effort of 227 from their full allotment of 50 overs.
The skipper put on an unbroken fifth-wicket partnership of 150 off 195 balls with Hashan Tillekaratne, who made an unbeaten 47.
The pair came together in just the 12th over when the Sri Lankan top order had hit out at some cost to see the game hanging in the balance with the visitors on 78 for four.
But Ranatunga and Tillekaratne steadied the tourists' progress, batted intelligently and punished anything loose.
The Sri Lankan innings began in frenetic fashion despite the loss of Sanath Jayasuriya in the opening over for a duck when New Zealand squad member Andrew Penn trapped him leg before wicket.
The abrupt departure of Jayasuriya, who had earlier performed outstandingly with the ball to claim figures of five for 37, did not make the Sri Lankans flinch.

Romesh Kaluwitharana thrashed 21 from 13 deliveries before he dabbled outside off stump to offer a catch behind from Craig Findlay, and then Aravinda de Silva quickly got into his stride as the tourists raced past 50 in the ninth over.

Following a horrendous run of form during the test series against New Zealand, when he pieced together just nine runs in four innings, de Silva looked a new man, displaying raw power and deft placement to speed to 34 from just 25 deliveries.

But after helping himself to six fours, and one six over mid wicket, de Silva fell to the innocuous medium pace of Nelson all-rounder Brent Williams who had the Sri Lankan kingpin caught by Penn at point.
It was Williams' second success after he had removed Marvan Atapattu with a superb yorker just four balls earlier.

At 78 for four in the 12th over, the run rate was of no concern to the tourists but they were dependent on captain Arjuna Ranatunga and Hashan Tillekaratne halting the fall of wickets and consolidating.
Jayasuriya, who normally destroys teams with the bat, inflicted damage with the ball.
Ranatunga was forced to turn to his slower bowlers after former international Craig Spearman threatened to destroy the Sri Lankan attack in the early stages.

Spearman caned his way to 56 from just 59 balls but Central Districts then had much to thank Matthew Sinclair for as he showed plenty of maturity in scoring a composed 67 before departing in the 48th over.
After their strong start Central Districts lost their way as Jayasuriya and leg-spinner Upul Chandana, who claimed three for 37, imposed tight control and subtle variations.
